long_biography.plain_text:
Ted Waitt helped scientists obtain tools and early funding through two distinct programmes. His foundation supported the creation of the Waitt Advanced Biophotonics Center at the Salk Institute. It gave researchers access to microscopes, imaging systems and technical support for studying the inner workings of living cells.

A partnership with National Geographic addressed an earlier obstacle: getting exploratory research started. Its grants programme backed fieldwork and proof-of-concept projects, including work by researchers near the beginning of their careers. Applications were considered throughout the year, with awards generally made within eight to twelve weeks. The programme supported almost 300 field projects before closing.
